decision: Adjacency-list tree for department (parent_id FK, cycle guard in app layer), single employee table polymorphic on kind ∈ {human,agent} (service fixture type maps to 'agent'), dev-seed block inside migrations 013-016 sourced from ORG_SEED, new DB access layer src/db/org.ts (listOrgTree, findEmployeeById, listHumanEmployees) behind existing src/http/org.ts exports (findEmployee/listSelectableUsers signatures preserved for frozen callers auth.ts/inbox.ts). Three test seams break and are owned by coder/BUILD: two_tenant.test.ts migration count 10→16, schema.test.ts FK pairs assertion expanded from 2 to 6, cross_tenant.test.ts seedRowForTable gains 4 new cases.

rejected_alternatives.why_not: Requires non-standard CREATE EXTENSION; tests must run on vanilla PG. Adjacency-list + recursive CTE is zero-extension and proportional to expected depth (<=5).
Adds a second table and multi-row write protocol for every department mutation. Over-engineering at expected scale; adjacency-list with recursive CTE is sufficient.
Violates spec invariant FR-4 and analyst decision (§6); doubles T-0022 join surface; finer AI-vs-connector distinction belongs in agent_card (T-0020). Rejected by spec.
Less extensible than kind text CHECK; if a third kind is added, boolean becomes a migration. text CHECK is spec-mandated shape.
Creates a second bring-up path violating T-0053 NF-4 one-path principle. Seeds stay in migrations 013-016 behind ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING.
src/core/ holds domain logic and store abstractions; org queries are HTTP-layer I/O. src/db/ is the correct layer for DB query modules backing HTTP routes.

rejected_alternatives.option: Generate new UUIDs for employee IDs (replace slugs)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Breaks Keycloak JWT→employee resolution chain (T-0054: employee.slug = jwt.preferred_username). Slugs are frozen identity keys.

rejected_alternatives.option: Position hierarchy (positions hang off other positions)
rejected_alternatives.why_not: Explicitly out of scope per spec §4. Positions hang off departments only.

contracts: Migration 013: CREATE TABLE choros.tenant (tenant_id uuid NOT NULL, id uuid NOT NULL, slug text NOT NULL, display_name text NOT NULL, created_at bigint NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, id), UNIQUE (slug)); RLS USING (id = current_setting('choros.tenant_id', true)::uuid); dev seed slug='dev'.

Migration 014: CREATE TABLE choros.department (..., parent_id uuid NULL, FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, parent_id) REFERENCES choros.department(tenant_id, id), FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, id) REFERENCES choros.tenant(tenant_id, id)); RLS; dev seed 3 root departments.
Migration 015: CREATE TABLE choros.position (..., FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, department_id) REFERENCES choros.department(tenant_id, id)); RLS; dev seed 8 positions.

Migration 016: CREATE TABLE choros.employee (..., kind text NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('human', 'agent')), FOREIGN KEY (tenant_id, position_id) REFERENCES choros.position(tenant_id, id)); RLS; dev seed 12 employees.
src/db/org.ts exports: listOrgTree(pool, tenantId), findEmployeeById(pool, tenantId, slug), listHumanEmployees(pool, tenantId) — async, use SET LOCAL choros.tenant_id inside transactions.
src/http/org.ts: findEmployee(id) and listSelectableUsers() signatures preserved; internally delegate to src/db/org.ts when DATABASE_URL set. No import-path changes for auth.ts/inbox.ts.
GET /api/org response shape: { departments: [{ id, name, positions: [{ id, title, people: [{ id, name, type }] }] }] }. type = employee.kind ('human' | 'agent').
GET /api/me dev-auth resolves against real employee table via slug lookup; unknown slug → 401.
